name: Continuity Social Hub
intent: A whole-ecosystem social hub whose visual grammar comes from modern feed, thread, composer, navigation, and activity surfaces. Semantic movement anchors remain an underlying words/pipes layer and are not exposed as the homepage visual taxonomy.

witnesses.notes: Reply, mention, quote/repost, and thread mechanics expose OPEN/PING/REPLY/ECHO/BRANCH relations.
Root posts, nested discussion, and reposting preserve source while opening a new audience/context.
One activity surface aggregates unlike movement types while preserving their distinctions and source context.
Open conversations can remain conversational or move into scoped work without requiring the conversation surface to become the work system.

layout.shape: three-zone social hub: persistent navigation, central feed/composer, contextual activity/sidebar
layout.source_treatment: source systems appear as identity/context on feed entries, not as separate dashboard cards
layout.branching: replies and threads visually retain parent context
layout.return_paths: notifications/activity reopen the relevant conversation in context

controls.composer: single social-style composer at the feed front
controls.quick_actions: conventional social controls such as reply, react, share/send, save, and open thread

surface.cards: feed entries rather than dashboard metric cards
surface.color: neutral base; movement/source chips carry restrained functional differentiation

motion.rule: new movement may enter the feed without decorative animation or attention theft

avoid: word-anchor rails or exposing internal movement taxonomy as homepage navigation
school-first navigation on the ecosystem homepage
one card per subsystem as the primary information architecture
flattening every movement into a task
social engagement scores, follower counts, streaks, or gamification
hiding source provenance when movement crosses systems
ornamental AI gradients, glow, or excessive glass effects
adaptation_rules: Treat Online School, Personal Operations, Calendar, Factory, research, jobs, and future systems as sources contributing entries to the same hub.
Preserve source-system ownership and provenance on each entry.
Keep semantic Words Movement anchors below the visual layer; do not render the anchor bank as navigation, badges, or visual taxonomy.
Calendar contributes time/context to entries but does not organize the homepage.
A conversation becomes scoped work only through an explicit backend transition; visually it remains a conversation until that transition is represented.
Use standard social-feed affordances so people can understand the surface without learning the internal movement vocabulary.

review.notes: Main ecosystem social-hub visual template. Internal Words Movement anchors remain backend semantics and are intentionally absent from the visual grammar.
